title: Exactness on each graded piece of the symmetric algebra of a quotient
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and let M_2 --a--> M_1 --p--> M -> 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules (so p is surjective and ker(p) = im(a)). For every integer n >= 1, the natural sequence of R-modules M_2 tensor_R Sym_R^{n-1}(M_1) -> Sym_R^n(M_1) -> Sym_R^n(M), whose first map sends y tensor s to iota(a(y)) times s and whose second map is induced by p, is exact; in particular, the second map is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241), the degree-n exact sequence for an exact sequence M_2 -> M_1 -> M -> 0
